messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: routing-router-east-1 latency > 95th pct threshold (2min spike) — PD INCIDENT #INC-48291 https://pagerduty.example/INC-48291 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident INC-48291 triggered (High). Acknowledgements required. Escalation policy: eng-oncall-primary.
maya: acked. i'm looking at router metrics now — seeing a ~300ms tail on request latency for 60-90s, request rate normal.
ops-sre: any customer-facing errors? error budget dashboards?
maya: no 5xx increase on the surface, just latency. traces show increased KV cache misses on prefix cache (kv-cache-east).
dmitri: fyi i'm up, moving to join. can we confirm if it's kv warmup or an autoscaler bounce?
maya: no autoscale events in the window, look at kv-cache miss rate graph: `kv_cache.miss_rate{region=east}` jumps at 22:11:08.
alex: pinging infra: the warmup worker logs show a flurry of TTL evictions around 22:09-22:10, could be a garbage collect sweep.
dmitri: ok, mitigation plan: temporarily route a small % of traffic to standby pool and increase kv-cache warmup concurrency. doing `curl -X POST https://internal-control/routing -d '{"route_shift": 0.1}'`
maya: on it — toggled rollout to shift 10% to standby for 3m.
ops-sre: also bumping warmup workers from 2->6 for east region: `kubectl scale deploy/kv-warmup -n infra --replicas=6`
incident-bot: NOTE: user-facing impact flag = false (no 5xx spike) — continue monitoring.
pagerduty-bot: INC-48291 acknowledged by maya at 22:12:04.
maya: seeing latency tail drop back toward baseline at 22:12:40. kv miss rate trending down.
dmitri: warming caches manually for hot prefixes that show high miss rate: `for p in $(cat hot_prefixes); do warmup-tool --prefix $p & done`
alex: logs confirm reduced miss rates. router p50/p95 improving.
ops-sre: rollback of routing shift in 90s?
maya: yes i'll revert shift after 3m window. queued revert at 22:15:12.
pagerduty-bot: INC-48291 auto-resolved at 22:13:11 (alert threshold cleared) — no further on-call actions required.
dmitri: nice. follow-up: file a short postmortem/ops note to investigate GC/eviction pattern and whether warmup concurrency should auto-scale on miss spikes.
maya: filing ops ticket now: OPS-2397 "kv-cache eviction burst -> transient latency" with timeline and graphs.
alex: thumbs — will add logs from warmup workers.
ops-sre: leaving a quick handoff note: i'm wrapping up and handing back to maya for any follow-ups tomorrow.
maya: thanks — marking thread resolved. no customer impact; PD incident closed. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Thread closed by maya at 22:16:31.
